content: I need to set better boundaries around on-call. Last week I got paged three times between midnight and 6am and I was completely useless the next day. The alerts were all for things that could have waited until morning.

Sounds like your alert severity levels need tuning. Pages that wake people up should only be for customer-impacting issues that need immediate action. Everything else should be a next-business-day ticket.

That's exactly right. We have alerts firing on things like 'disk usage above 70%' at 2am — that's not an emergency, that's a Tuesday morning task. The thing is, the team is afraid to downgrade alerts because we once missed a real outage that started as a disk warning.
That's a common fear. The solution is better alert design, not more pages. A disk at 70% gets a ticket. A disk at 90% and growing gets a page. The first gives you time, the second demands action.

Fundamentally we need to distinguish between signals that need human intervention right now versus signals that need human attention during business hours. I'm going to propose a two-tier on-call: page-worthy and ticket-worthy, with clear criteria for each.
Two-tier with documented criteria is the standard approach. Google's SRE book has a good framework for this — the page should answer 'what action do I need to take right now that can't wait 8 hours?'

Yeah, and if the answer is 'nothing' then it shouldn't have woken me up. I'm also going to push for an on-call handoff meeting every Monday where the outgoing person briefs the incoming person on active issues. We keep losing context across rotations.
